does: Lets water or oil run off food after it has been boiled, soaked, salted or fried, so that it is not watery or greasy when it meets the next step.

intro.what: Water or oil is allowed to run off food before it enters the next stage.
intro.why: Residual liquid can dilute a sauce or soften a crust. The draining surface should suit the food rather than trap liquid beneath it.

how: Tip boiled food into a colander set in the sink, and give it a good shake. Keep a ladleful of the cooking water if the dish will want it.
Leave soaked or salted food in a colander for a while, and press out the rest of the water with the hands or a cloth.
Lift fried food out with a slotted spoon and set it on a rack or on paper.
Shake or toss the food once to free the last of the liquid.

cues.text: No more drops fall from the food.
The food is no longer slippery with water, and fried pieces feel dry and light.

mistakes.mistake: Draining fried food flat on a plate, where it steams and goes soft.
mistakes.fix: Set it on a rack, or on paper that is changed when it soaks through.

mistakes.mistake: Throwing away all the cooking water of pasta, when the dish needs it to loosen a sauce.
Draining too little, so that the food waters down the dish.
mistakes.fix: Shake it well, and press out what a cloth can take.

quiz.question: Why drain before combining food with the next mixture?
choices: To add more loose liquid without measuring it.
To avoid carrying unwanted water or oil into it.
To make every surface absorb extra moisture.
quiz.because: Liquid left clinging to the food can change the consistency of the next mixture.

quiz.question: What should happen before draining pasta if its sauce needs cooking water?
choices: Discard all the cooking water immediately.
Rinse the pasta until no starch remains.
Reserve some of the cooking water first.
quiz.because: Reserving the useful liquid keeps it available for adjusting the sauce afterward.

quiz.question: Which cue suggests loose liquid has drained away?
choices: Drops have stopped falling from the food.
Liquid still streams from the food.
The food sits in a growing puddle.
quiz.because: The end of dripping indicates that the freely running liquid has left.

quiz.question: Fried food softens while lying flat in pooled liquid. What should change?
choices: Leave it in the puddle beneath a cover.
Drain it on a rack or suitable absorbent paper.
Stack it tightly on the same wet plate.
quiz.because: Separating the food from collected liquid limits the steaming that softens its crust.
